* [[Dutch general election, 2006|Early elections in November]] are announced in the [[Netherlands]]. [http://today.reuters.co.uk/news/newsArticle.aspx?type=worldNews&storyID=2006-07-01T164748Z_01_L01590420_RTRUKOC_0_UK-DUTCH-ELECTIONS.xml&archived=False (Reuters)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
* [[Effects of Hurricane Katrina on New Orleans]]:
** [[Six Flags]] announces that [[Six Flags New Orleans|its New Orleans]] [[amusement park]] in [[Louisiana]], which has been closed since [[Hurricane Katrina]] struck the previous year, will not reopen and that it is seeking to terminate its 75-year lease with [[New Orleans|the city]]. [https://www.wafb.com/story/5104570/six-flags-wants-out-of-new-orleans-agreement/ (WAFB)] [https://web.archive.org/web/20090215101618/https://www.nola.com/news/t-p/frontpage/index.ssf?/base/news-6/1151735344140970.xml&coll=1 (''The Times-Picayune'')]
* [[Space Shuttle Discovery|Discovery]] Mission [[STS-121]]'s launch has been delayed today due to thunderstorms. The next launch attempt is scheduled for 3:26 PM EDT tomorrow, although more bad weather is forecast.[http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/shuttle/main/index.html (NASA)][http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/stories/S/SPACE_SHUTTLE?SITE=7219&SECTION=HOME&TEMPLATE=DEFAULT&CTIME=2006-07-01-15-51-21 (Associated Press)] 
* [[Osama Bin Laden]] warns the US and other nations not to become involved in [[Somalia]] and says that [[Al Qaeda]] reserves the right to "punish" the U.S. on its own soil. [https://web.archive.org/web/20051221183105/http://go.reuters.co.uk/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews (Reuters)]
* The [[United Nations Security Council]] [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 1692|votes unanimously]] to withdraw the 3,500 [[United Nations Operation in Burundi|peacekeeping troops]] who are currently in [[Burundi]] on [[December 31]], despite the continuing activities of the [[National Forces of Liberation|National Liberation Force]] [[Rebellion|rebel]] group. [https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20060701/ap_on_re_af/un_burundi_1 (Reuters)]
* At least 60 people die from a car bomb in a market in [[Sadr City]], a Shiite district of [[Baghdad]]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20061120195641/http://www.turkishpress.com/news.asp?id=131363 (Turkish Press)]
* The [[Qingzang railway]] is formally opened in the by [[President_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China|Chinese President]] [[Hu Jintao]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/5133220.stm (BBC)]
* [[Operation Summer Rains]]:
** An Israeli helicopter gunship attacks the office of [[Prime Minister of Palestine]] [[Ismail Haniyeh]]. Observers report that the building had been set on fire but was unoccupied. [http://www.theage.com.au/news/World/Palestinian-PMs-office-targeted/2006/07/02/1151778796000.html (Melbourne Age)]
** [[Israel]] rejects demand to free 1,000 prisoners, delivered earlier by the [[Hamas|abductors]] of Cpl. [[Gilad Shalit]]. A [[Palestinian National Authority|Palestenian]] deputy minister says Shalit is in stable condition, but no sign of life is yet given. [https://web.archive.org/web/20060703205429/http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/733349.html (Haaretz)]
** ''[[The Australian]]'' reports [[Israel]] threatens to assassinate [[Palestinian National Authority|Palestinian]] [[Prime Minister]] [[Ismail Haniyeh]] unless Israel's kidnapped soldier, [[Gilad Shalit]], is released unharmed. No other news source confirms this report. [https://web.archive.org/web/20070527010944/http://www.theaustralian.news.com.au/story/0%2C20867%2C19645805-601%2C00.html (The Australian)]
* A ceremony is held at [[Thiepval]], [[Picardy]], in [[France]], to commemorate the 90th anniversary of the [[Battle of the Somme]].  ([http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/5135878.stm BBC])
